cards.explanation: The answer is True. Israel says to David at Hebron, "Here we are, your own flesh and blood." (1 Chronicles 11:1) They show up and claim David as family. I think that's the kind of welcome a man remembers.

The answer is a shepherd for His people. The people say the LORD told David, "You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them." (1 Chronicles 11:2) So he's a shepherd and a ruler. Notice it says "My people." They belong to the LORD, and David looks after them, friends.

The answer is covenant. David "…made a covenant with them before the LORD." (1 Chronicles 11:3) A covenant is a serious agreement, and this one is made in front of the LORD. That's no handshake over a cookie box, friends.
The answer is they anoint him. "And they anointed him king over Israel…" (1 Chronicles 11:3) The elders anoint David to make him king. Anointing is how the job gets made official.

The answer is True. The anointing happens "…according to the word of the LORD through Samuel." (1 Chronicles 11:3) The LORD's word came through Samuel, and the elders are acting in line with it, bakers.
The answer is "You will never get in here." The people of Jebus tell David exactly that. (1 Chronicles 11:5) Hold onto that line, friends, because the very same verse has an answer for it.

The answer is False. After the people of Jebus say, "You will never get in here." the text says, "Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David)." (1 Chronicles 11:5) That "nevertheless" turns the whole scene around. They said never, and the verse says David captured it.

The answer is he becomes chief commander. David says, "Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander." (1 Chronicles 11:6) That's a big promotion for one first move, friends. Somebody was about to get a new title.

The answer is True. "…Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief." (1 Chronicles 11:6) David had said, "Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander." David put the job on the table, and Joab went up first. Me? I'd have been the one asking who goes second.

The answer is David. "So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David." (1 Chronicles 11:7) The king moves in and the fortress takes his name. The text also calls the fortress of Zion the City of David. My name's carved on my handle, so I know how good it feels to have your name on something.

The answer is True. David "…built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city." (1 Chronicles 11:8) David builds up the city around the fortress, and Joab restores the rest. So each of them has a part in the work, friends.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts is with him. "And David became greater and greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him." (1 Chronicles 11:9) The text gives the reason right there, bakers. It's not about what David had, it's about who was with him.
